title: yaah workflow validate --json report
description: JSON report emitted by 'yaah workflow validate --json <spec>' (cmd/yaah/workflow_report.go, kind yaah.workflow.validate.v1). The shape is stable within v1. errors and warnings serialize as [] (never null). A report always goes to stdout when --json is set — including load failures — with the summary line on stderr. Exit code is 0 when ok is true and 1 otherwise.

kind.description: Report kind discriminator; bumped only on a breaking shape change.

spec.description: The spec path exactly as given on the command line.

name.description: Workflow name from the document (omitted when the document never decoded).

status.description: The document's verdict, independent of --strict: valid = decoded, resolved, and no error findings; invalid = decoded and resolved into a graph but carries error findings (status=invalid always implies a non-empty errors array); unresolved = load, decode, param, or ir.Resolve failed, so node-level families (WF002-WF036) could not run and the failure is reported as a synthetic diagnostic.

ok.description: Final verdict after --strict promotion: true iff no errors and (no warnings or not strict). --strict flips ok and the exit code; it never rewrites status.

errors.description: Error-severity findings, canonical rule order. Every error code is document-intrinsic — true on every host (WF001-WF029, WF034, WF036).

warnings.description: Warning-severity findings: the host-relative codes WF030 (role registry), WF031 (world registry; its document-intrinsic halves stay warnings for whole-code consistency — the code is the contract), WF032 (network ceiling), WF033 (dispatch budget), WF035 (configured caps). --strict promotes them to failure via ok and the exit code without moving them out of this array.

code.description: Stable rule code from the internal/workflow/validate catalog (see its doc.go).

path.description: Dotted spec path the finding points at (omitted for document-level findings).
